test_title: SSC Selection Post Matric Level Official Paper (Held on: 1 Aug 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: A farmer counted the heads of the animals and birds on the farm and found it to be 40. When he counted the legs, he found it to be 120. If the farm had either pigeons or horses and nothing else, how many horses were there on the farm? On the farm, each horse had four legs and each pigeon had two legs.
solution:
**Given:**

A farmer counted the heads of the animals and birds on the farm and found it to be 40. 

When he counted the legs, he found it to be 120

**Calculations:**

According to the question,

The count of heads gives the total number of animals / birds as each animal / bird has one head.

Let the number of horses be x.

The remaining will be pigeons.

The number of pigeons = (40 - x).

Each pigeon has 2 legs and each horse has 4 legs.

Therefore, total number of legs = 4x + 2(40 - x) = 120

4x + 80 - 2x = 120

⇒ 2x = 120 - 80

⇒ 2x = 40

⇒ x = 20.

∴ The number of horses in the farm is 20.
